additional_concerns: Paragraph 10 supports continuing ultimate responsibility, but does not itself establish the candidate's complete conjunctive test of retained authority, supervision and satisfactory outcomes. The applicable performance standard, assessment period, incident severity, duration and remediation rules remain unresolved.

Proper ownership records and operational compatibility are expressly required by s2. Neither accurate vendor records alone nor retained authority alone establishes full substantive discharge. The excerpts do not establish a universal no-failure guarantee or permit treating missing evidence as substantive failure.

Paragraph 14 in s3 most naturally attaches the SFC-request trigger to demonstration while leaving confirmation unqualified. Footnote 5 in s4 specifies minimum content; its standalone wording also permits an unresolved broader demonstration reading. SFC satisfaction and high confidence concerning smart-contract flaws should not automatically become paragraph 10's general performance standard.

Absent an SFC request, the express procurement triggers in paragraphs 15 and 16 are not met. Paragraph 16 concerns a satisfactory legal opinion supporting the application; paragraph 15 concerns third-party audit or verification. Neither procurement nor absence of a request establishes substantive compliance.

Complete paragraphs 10–13, footnote 2 and the applicable Appendix factors are not supplied. Actual authority allocations, appointments, supervision, operational incidents and ownership-record evidence are also absent.
The candidate has no executable formalization. Retrieval success and the supplied structural-tool results establish neither legal applicability nor executable fidelity.
